title: Binary and Denary
intro: Catch up with the essential learning in about 10–15 minutes. Complete five short steps and check your answers as you go.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Start with two familiar facts about computer data.

questions.prompt: Which two digits are used in binary?
questions.feedback: Binary means base two, so it uses only 0 and 1.

questions.prompt: How many bits make one byte?
questions.feedback: Eight individual bits make a byte.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Learn binary place values and how to convert numbers.

blocks.title: Why binary?
blocks.text: Digital circuits can reliably represent two states, often called off and on. Binary uses 0 and 1. A bit is one binary digit; denary is base ten.

items: Eight-bit positions from left to right: 128 · 64 · 32 · 16 · 8 · 4 · 2 · 1
For binary → denary, add place values wherever a bit is 1.
For denary → binary, choose place values that add to the number and fill remaining bits with 0.
Unsigned eight-bit values run from 0 to 255: there are 2⁸ = 256 possible patterns, including zero.

blocks.title: Worked example · denary → binary
blocks.text: 154 = 128 + 16 + 8 + 2, so its eight-bit binary form is 10011010.

questions.prompt: What is the value of the leftmost (most significant) bit in an eight-bit unsigned number?
questions.feedback: The place values start at 128 on the left.

questions.prompt: Why is the largest unsigned eight-bit value 255 rather than 256?

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Convert numbers and organise the method.

blocks.text: Eight bits must be shown, including leading zeros when needed.

questions.prompt: Match each binary pattern to its denary value.
questions.feedback: Each position has its own power-of-two place value.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for converting denary 154 to binary in order.
Convert denary 178 into an eight-bit binary value (enter eight digits).

stages.label: Apply
stages.lead: Code First and one written exam-style explanation.

blocks.title: Code First · Predict → Write → Test → Improve
blocks.caption: Predict the output. Change the expression to add 8 + 2 for the binary pattern 1010.

blocks.text: Written question: Explain how you would convert the denary number 191 to unsigned eight-bit binary. Include the place values and the resulting bits.

questions.feedback: The expression adds 8, 2 and 1, resulting in 11.
The binary place values 8 and 2 total 10.

questions.prompt: Convert denary 154 to eight-bit binary (enter all eight digits).

writing.prompt: Write two or three sentences explaining your conversion.
writing.model: 191 = 128 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1. Put a 1 in each of these columns and a 0 in the 64 column, giving unsigned eight-bit binary 10111111.
checklist: I identified the eight binary place values.
I gave the eight-bit answer 10111111 and corrected any errors.

stages.label: Check
stages.lead: Finish with three quick checks and review your mastery.

questions.prompt: An unsigned eight-bit number can represent denary 256.
questions.feedback: False: the largest unsigned eight-bit value is 255.

questions.prompt: The binary number 10000000 is 128 in denary.
questions.feedback: True: only the 128 column contains a 1.

questions.prompt: Converting denary to binary changes the number's value.
questions.feedback: False: the value stays the same; only the representation changes.
